video_title: Micah Nori Postgame Interview | Portland Trail Blazers 103, San Antonio Spurs 125 | Nov. 7, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the Trail Blazers' poor start and defensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: I thought we defended well the end of the first quarter, we couldn't buy a bucket.
quotes.quote: Most frustrating was we just talked about the start. They're coming in here on a back-to-back as well, and they go up 11-3. I thought we defended well the end of the first quarter, we couldn't buy a bucket, really struggled to make shots. And then the second quarter we just didn't give ourselves a chance, quite honestly. Quite a few turnovers and then we put them on the free throw line 18 times. They are fouls, and you just can't have them. And then they go 28-for-30, again, 18 of them in the second quarter. And then it just felt like the game never got ourselves back in the game.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the Blazers' loss to the Spurs: We just did not give ourselves a chance. Too many turnovers and we put them on the free throw line 18 times in the second quarter alone.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the Trail Blazers' poor start and defensive struggles in a loss to the Spurs.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori emphasizes the need for consistent competitiveness despite injuries
quotes.excerpt: We're going to have guys out, I don't care who's out, we got to make sure we compete.
quotes.quote: Told the guys, everybody, if you want to find an excuse, you can find an excuse, but it's a big-boy league. They're on a back-to-back, we're on a back-to-back, these are going to happen. We're going to have guys out, I don't care who's out, we got to make sure we compete and be who we are. And tonight I thought was the first time that we kind of got away from that. I know that they were doing some things with their physicality that got us frustrated, and so I guess there's a lot that bothered me, quite honestly.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the Blazers' effort tonight: It is a big boy league. I do not care who is out, we have to make sure we compete and be who we are. Tonight was the first time we got away from that.

structured.context: Micah Nori emphasizes the need for his team to maintain competitiveness despite dealing with player absences.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on defensive adjustments against Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: Wembanyama's big, they crash, you got to hit them early.
quotes.quote: Some of them are after the shot goes up, the offensive rebounds. Wembanyama's big, they crash, you got to hit them early. So you got to make sure you meet them outside the restricted area, because once he gets inside the restricted area, it's a problem. And then just a couple of times, just a couple mental lapses, we go under Champagnie a couple times, he makes two of those threes right in a row. But then I just thought that was the first time we just got a little bit frustrated and gave in a little bit.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on defending Victor Wembanyama: You have to meet him outside the restricted area, because once he gets inside the restricted area, it is a problem.

structured.context: Micah Nori explains the defensive challenges posed by Victor Wembanyama and Julian Champagnie during the game.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori rejects the idea that the loss is a 'humble pie' moment
quotes.excerpt: I don't consider it a wake-up call, but I don't think it necessarily that humble pie.
quotes.quote: I don't consider it a wake-up call, but I don't think it necessarily that humble pie. I mean, they beat us. I don't know what humble pie means from the fact that we've played really good basketball and we're 6-2, and there's not one person on our team that thought that, you know, thinking that all of a sudden we're world beaters and all this. I think we've been going about our business, taking care of business on the road, and the last thing I would think about this is humble pie. I think that they're a very good team, they're the defending Western Conference champions and they beat us.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori rejects the idea that tonight's loss was a wake-up call or humble pie for the 6-2 Blazers: They are a very good team, they are the defending Western Conference champions and they beat us.

structured.context: Micah Nori rejects the idea that the loss to the Spurs serves as a wake-up call for his team.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori explains the logic behind using smaller lineups against Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: The logic there was just to try to play the analytics a little bit.
quotes.quote: The logic there was just to try to play the analytics a little bit and see what it looks like and make Castle make shots. And you know, he goes 2-for-5 and finds a way to get five assists. So that was the logic there and try to keep Donovan at the rim a little bit more. And had a little bit of success with it in small doses in Denver when we put the two smalls on Jokic. But that's what that was, just to see what it looked like.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori explains the decision to use smaller lineups against the Spurs: The logic was to try to play the analytics a little bit and make Castle make shots.

structured.context: Micah Nori explains the strategic logic behind using smaller lineups to defend Victor Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the impact of playoff experience against smaller lineups
quotes.excerpt: We also played them in Minnesota and played them and then, you know, little PTSD.
quotes.quote: For sure, I mean, I did. But we also played them in Minnesota and played them and then, you know, little PTSD because we tried this in Game 6 last year and put Rudy on Castle. And the analytics say it's a good matchup and he had 32 points and we lost 139 to 109. So, but expected, that's kind of what you go with a little bit. You just when you put your game plan together, you're just trying to see what you can do to make things a little bit difficult for them.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori admits to some PTSD regarding defensive schemes against Stephon Castle: The analytics say it is a good matchup, but we tried this in Game 6 last year and he had 32 points and we lost 139 to 109.

structured.context: Micah Nori reflects on past defensive adjustments against Stephon Castle and how they influenced his current game plan.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori evaluates Hansel's performance and need for continued development
quotes.excerpt: I thought that Hansel was fine, he goes, played 26 minutes, found a way to get 10 rebounds.
quotes.quote: I thought that Hansel was fine, he goes, played 26 minutes, found a way to get 10 rebounds. And he's fine, gets to the free throw line six times, shots some open shots. We just need him to continue to to get better. And I think the more that he continues to play and he starts to play well and and gets sped up and everything and his communication gets better, that that's only a positive for us. So the more minutes that he can gain, the better that we will reap the benefits of for moving forward.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on the development of Hansel: He played 26 minutes and found a way to get 10 rebounds. We just need him to continue to get better and his communication to get better.

structured.context: Micah Nori evaluates the performance of Hansel Enmanuel and discusses his need for continued development.
